title: Risk Profiling Questionnaire
description: DOCX-aligned typed questionnaire for liquidity capture and automatic investor-profile scoring. Liquidity answers are handled separately from risk scoring.

questions.text: How much are you investing in this portfolio today? The minimum portfolio value for this questionnaire is $25,000.
questions.help_text: You can type a plain number or include a dollar sign and commas, for example: $50,000.

questions.text: How much might you need to withdraw for a major expense in the next 12 to 24 months?
questions.help_text: Use 0 if no major withdrawal is expected.

questions.text: What are your estimated essential monthly expenses?
questions.help_text: This helps estimate the Cash amount that should remain available for near-term liquidity.

questions.text: How many months of expenses would you like to have set aside for emergencies?
questions.help_text: This is used for the liquidity calculation, not the risk-bucket score.

questions.text: How many months of expenses have you currently set aside for emergencies?
questions.help_text: This is a risk-capacity signal: stronger current reserves generally support more risk capacity.

questions.text: How would you describe your non-investment income?
questions.help_text: More stable income generally increases the capacity to hold through market volatility.

options.label: Very stable
options.description: Stable job or reliable income with high surplus.

options.label: Moderately stable
options.description: Standard employment or moderately predictable income.

options.label: Unstable
options.description: Variable income, commission-based income, or uncertain employment.

questions.text: To what extent do others depend on your income or financial resources for ongoing support?
questions.help_text: Higher obligations reduce risk capacity because more people rely on the investor's income.

options.label: At least three dependents rely heavily on my income
options.description: I am the sole or main breadwinner for several people.

options.label: Two or more people depend on my income
options.description: I have meaningful ongoing support obligations.

options.label: I have little to no financial dependence obligations
options.description: Few or no people rely on my income for ongoing support.

questions.text: When do you expect to need a large amount of money from these investments?
questions.help_text: Longer time horizons generally support more risk capacity.

questions.text: What phase of your investment life would you say you are in?
questions.help_text: Accumulation usually supports more risk capacity than drawing from the portfolio.

options.label: Capital disbursement
options.description: The portfolio is being used more directly for withdrawals.

options.label: Capital accumulation
options.description: The portfolio is still mainly for growth.

questions.text: If the stock market dropped 25% tomorrow and stayed there for two years, what would you do?
questions.help_text: This is the main drawdown-reaction question. Selling everything caps the calculated profile at Balanced.

options.label: Sell everything to protect what is left
options.description: Exit the position after a major drop.

options.label: Sell a portion and move to a safer investment
Do nothing / stay invested
options.description: Hold the portfolio through the decline.

options.label: Invest more to take advantage of lower prices

questions.text: How willing are you to accept short-term losses for potential long-term gain?
questions.help_text: This captures return-seeking preference and comfort with temporary losses.

options.label: Willing
options.description: Comfortable with some losses for long-term gain.

options.label: Indifferent
options.description: Neutral on short-term losses versus long-term gain.

options.label: Very unwilling
options.description: Strongly prefers to avoid short-term losses.

questions.text: How knowledgeable are you about financial and investment concepts?
questions.help_text: This is treated as a behavioural-consistency support signal, not a guarantee of discipline.

options.label: Limited investment knowledge
options.description: Very limited familiarity with finance and investing.

questions.text: How long have you been investing?
questions.help_text: This is also treated as a behavioural-consistency support signal.

questions.text: An investor chooses a portfolio expected to produce higher long-term returns but with larger temporary declines. Six months later, the portfolio falls by 30% during a market downturn. What would you think?
questions.help_text: This captures loss aversion in a scenario that every user can answer, even without prior investing experience.

options.label: I should move to safer investments before losses worsen.
I may have taken more risk than I am comfortable with.
Market declines are uncomfortable but expected.
This may be an opportunity to invest more.
options.description: Sees the decline as a buying opportunity.
